correctness.rationale: Symmetry averaging preserves the zero diagonal and reduces all feasible weights to a scalar q. Fourier layer modes have eigenvalues 1-q lambda and -1+q(4-lambda). On odd cycles the top and bottom antisymmetric modes give a sharp lower bound balanced uniquely by q=2/(4+epsilon); explicit endpoint inequalities bound all remaining modes. On even cycles the bipartition sign vector is a universal -1 eigenvector. Asymptotic Taylor expansion proves the factor-four spectral gap difference. 24,892 finite numerical assertions corroborate the formulas but do not substitute for proof.

value.rationale: Zero holding is a natural constraint for synchronous token/traffic movement, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The theorem gives exact optimal transition probabilities for every odd prism and proves that even prisms can never mix under this restriction. The optimal odd-size gap is four times smaller asymptotically than when holding is allowed. This is a complete natural network-design invariant not implied by the previous unconstrained optimum.
